transcript: The open secret of this play, if it's even a secret at all, is that it's based on a true story of domestic vioIence perpetrated by an actor who still has a thriving career on stage and screen. But even with that elephant in the room, or maybe even because of it, the playwright seems to deliberately emphasize that this is not about any one abuser or any one victim. The unusual setup of this production is that multiple stars will take turns playing the lead role over the course of the run, from Lupita Nyong’o, Philippa Soo, Edie Falco. But the playwright herself, Marin Ireland, is notably not part of this lineup, despite being one of New York's most revered acting talents. And this casting format echoes a line in the play itself where the protagonist confesses begrudgingly that she never thought something like this could happen to someone “like her,” the truth, of course, being that this can happen to anyone. But beyond that, the play isn't even about the protagonist's relationship with the abuser. It's more about her relationship with everyone else. It's constructed as a series of interactions with her mother, a lawyer, a mutual friend, a first date, in group therapy. And while the play definitely doesn't shy away from the thorny nuances of domestic vioIence specifically, in a different sense, it could be about any painful experience and getting used to the discomfort of speaking about it as a new, unavoidable fact of your life story: the awkward questions people ask, the jokes they think are lightening the mood, and the little unsolicited comments that subtly or not so subtly shift the blame back onto her. But she also gets into the complicated gray area of refusing to let this incident go despite not knowing what result she wants from it, especially when the perpetrator has already admitted fault and apologized. So she's left with this burning pain, but unsure what to channel it into. And the sun of these parts feels like a desperate attempt to articulate through drama what can't quite be articulated in daily life. Like she's addressing the people in her community asking how this has been for her, as if to say, “this 75 minute play is the simplest answer I can give” “So here you go.”
classificationReason: Present-tense critical analysis of the play's structure, themes, and casting format (Lupita Nyong'o, Philippa Soo, Edie Falco) with clear evaluative opinion throughout. Matches Pre-Existing Condition at Greenwich House.
